candidate.title: TruSeq RNA Access
candidate.scope: The assigned TruSeq RNA Access product schematic, from pooling already prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries through probe hybridization, streptavidin magnetic-bead capture and elution to a target-bearing library ready for cluster generation. Upstream RNA extraction and conversion into a sequencing library, and downstream cluster generation and sequencing, are outside the depicted operations. No alternative method or implementation version is named.

states.label: Prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries to be pooled
features: The top region shows multiple linear library molecules with colored end regions, including a molecule with a central region labeled Target.
The stated input is already a stranded RNA-Seq library; the diagram does not show the preparation of these molecules from biological RNA.

evidence.locator: Top library stack, Target label and Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries caption

states.label: Pool of stranded RNA-Seq library molecules
features: Multiple prepared libraries form the common input to probe hybridization.
Pooling combines library molecules; it does not itself attach the capture probe.

evidence.locator: Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries caption, plus sign above probe and downward arrow to hybridized target

states.label: Biotinylated target probe
features: Short blue target probe with an attached biotin symbol, identified by the Biotinylated target probe caption.
The probe is a capture reagent added to the library pool, not the final sequenced library molecule; its nucleic-acid composition and terminal attachment position are not specified.

evidence.locator: Plus sign and short blue probe with pendant symbol, Biotinylated target probe caption

states.label: Library target hybridized to a biotinylated probe
features: A short blue probe is drawn paired beneath the central target region of a full-length library molecule.
Biotin remains attached to the probe, while the target remains part of the library molecule with its flanking colored regions.

evidence.locator: Hybridize probes to targets row, central target/probe duplex with pendant symbol

states.label: Streptavidin magnetic beads
features: Solid capture support identified by the Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads caption.
The gray curved support and blue binding-site icons represent the capture interface, not separate sample compartments or additional biological targets.

evidence.locator: Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads caption and gray/blue support illustration

states.label: Target-bearing library tethered to streptavidin magnetic beads through its biotinylated probe
features: The library target remains hybridized to the probe; the pendant probe modification contacts the bead-associated binding interface.
Attachment to the solid support distinguishes this material from the preceding free hybrid; the full library molecule remains drawn above the support.

evidence.locator: Capture row: central target/probe assembly connected to the blue binding interface on the gray bead

states.label: Eluted target-bearing library ready for cluster generation
features: The final linear library is detached from the bead and has no capture probe drawn alongside it.
The labeled order from left to right is P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7; the central target and both index regions are physically carried on the same depicted library molecule.

This is interpreted as a DNA sequencing-library carrier of RNA-derived target information, rather than the biological RNA itself: the input is an already prepared RNA-Seq library and the output is labeled with P5/P7 and ready for cluster generation.
The schematic gives no gene identities, probe coverage, capture efficiency or demonstrated absence of off-target molecules.

evidence.locator: Bottom product row: P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7 and Product ready for cluster generation
Top Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries input and bottom P5/P7 cluster-ready product
evidence.rationale: The diagram begins after stranded RNA-Seq library preparation and ends with a P5/P7-bearing cluster-generation substrate. Together these labels support interpreting the selected physical carrier as an RNA-derived DNA sequencing library; no RNA-to-DNA reaction is depicted here.

operations.label: Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries
operations.description: Combine the already prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries into the common material that is presented to the target probe. The change is mixture membership, not a depicted alteration of library sequence or ends.
operations.information_effect: Target-bearing molecules enter a shared pool. The final product retains index regions, but index assignment to individual starting libraries is not shown.

evidence.locator: Top stack of library molecules and Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries caption

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: Add the biotinylated target probe to the pooled libraries and hybridize it to the library's target region. The output is a probe-library hybrid that retains the full target-bearing library molecule and carries the probe's biotin capture handle.
operations.mechanism: Target-probe hybridization, depicted as pairing of the short blue probe with the central target region.
operations.information_effect: The probe associates target recognition with a biotin capture handle. The target sequence remains in the pre-existing library molecule; no copying or replacement by a probe-derived sequencing product is depicted.

evidence.locator: Library-plus-probe assembly, downward arrow, and Hybridize probes to targets row

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads
operations.description: Capture the probe-library hybrid on streptavidin magnetic beads through the biotinylated probe. The previously free hybrid becomes a bead-associated target-bearing library complex.
operations.mechanism: The labeled biotinylated probe links the target hybrid to the labeled streptavidin bead interface.
operations.information_effect: Interpreted as affinity enrichment of library molecules recognized by the probe. The retained material carries the library target and flanking regions; the depiction does not establish perfect biological specificity or a quantitative enrichment factor.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from hybrid to Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads row, including probe-to-bead contact
Target hybridization followed by bead capture and recovery of a Target-labeled product
evidence.rationale: Coupling target hybridization to the probe's biotin-mediated bead attachment provides a route for preferential recovery of probe-recognized library molecules. No specificity or recovery measurement is displayed.

operations.label: Elute
operations.description: Release target-bearing library material from the depicted bead-associated complex. The output is a free library molecule bearing the target, index regions and P5/P7 ends, labeled ready for cluster generation; the capture probe and bead are absent from the product drawing.
operations.information_effect: The recovered library retains the central target sequence and its physical association with the flanking index and P5/P7 regions. Subsequent sequencing could read target-derived sequence from these recovered molecules; neither sequencing nor a quantitative RNA measurement is shown.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow beneath bead capture, Elute caption, and final labeled cluster-ready product
Final Target segment and Product ready for cluster generation caption
evidence.rationale: The target remains physically present in the cluster-ready library, supporting its use as the sequence readout carrier. The figure stops before generating any reads or expression estimates.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and diagram both identify TruSeq RNA Access as the sole target. All four operations belong to its depicted capture component. No named alternative, repeated independent branch or primary-paper association is supplied; this resolves the schematic's applicability without asserting a complete protocol or equivalence to another product.

evidence.locator: Card title and description_verbatim
TruSeq RNA Access title and complete downward workflow from pooled libraries to cluster-ready product

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete single-route extraction: prepared libraries are pooled, combined with a biotinylated probe, hybridized, captured on streptavidin magnetic beads, and eluted as a target-bearing cluster-ready library. All depicted transformations, reagent interfaces, attachment changes and final labels are represented by the seven states, four operations and ten flows. There is no omitted alternative or independently processed branch. The DNA-carrier interpretation is explicitly qualified as an inference. No primary publication is supplied or required for this source depiction, so empty paper_matches is appropriate; no paper chemistry or historical claim is asserted. No consequential correction or unresolved architecture question is needed.

There is no grouped target requiring an additional applicability or paper assessment.
